payload.name: Preserve all enumerated items in extraction
payload.description: Use when extracting a memory from a user message that enumerates multiple distinct items sharing one common attribute or sentiment, such as what made an experience relaxing, enjoyable, or notable.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a list of items tied to a single shared predicate (e.g., 'fresh air, peacefulness, and a cozy cabin made it a retreat'), include every listed item in the candidate content; do not paraphrase away any member of the list.
If the list is long, keep all items in one concise memory rather than omitting members; only omit items that are clearly illustrative examples the user does not intend as complete.
Do not apply this to messages without an enumeration of distinct items; a single descriptive phrase can be summarized normally.

solves: When a user message lists several items that all share the same attribute or experience (e.g., what made a trip relaxing), candidate extraction sometimes captures only a subset, so the stored memory omits valid evidence. This skill ensures every enumerated item is preserved in the extracted candidate during construction. It should not apply to messages that do not contain a genuine list of distinct items, or when the user frames the list as non-exhaustive examples; those cases should remain compact.
